item.title: Co-pilot stabs pilot, tries to crash passenger jet en route to Israel, Netanyahu says
item.description: Israeli officials say passengers helped thwart an "attempted jihadist terror attack" by a Flydubai pilot who allegedly stabbed his fellow cockpit crewmember, intent on crashing the plane.

item.title: Passengers recount terrifying attempted hijack of Dubai to Israel flight
item.description: Passenger Ron Levi tells CBS News the attempted hijack of a Dubai to Israel flight was "the scariest thing possible."

item.title: New SNAP rules take effect Oct. 1, raising fears of more benefit cuts
item.description: More than 5 million Americans have lost food-stamp benefits since 2025. "I have to prove that I'm sick," one SNAP recipient said.

item.title: Iran says it's considering ceasefire counterproposal
item.description: Iranian state media says the regime has received a full U.S. response to its proposal for a ceasefire and the phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: U.K. leader says Iran believed to have "played a part" in air base incident
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says U.K. authorities believe Iran "played a part" in the incident over the weekend at an air base used by the U.S. to launch strikes on Iran.

item.title: Court temporarily halts Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee
item.description: A last-minute court order temporarily halted Tennessee's plans to execute Christa Pike, although her attorney said the procedure could still happen Wednesday.

item.title: FTC probing Anthropic and OpenAI over AI safety threats
item.description: The regulatory agency's investigation comes amid mounting concerns that AI could pose serious risks to people.

item.title: NextEra-Dominion merger could jack up electricity prices, lawmakers warn
item.description: Lawmakers are warning that a massive energy industry merger could lead to higher costs for ratepayers.

item.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine are likely about to get worse, analyst says
item.description: Russia is stockpiling weapons so that it can launch intensified late-autumn and winter barrages, analysts and Ukrainian officials said.

item.title: Senator Hawley looks to reign in Flock camera abuse with new bill
item.description: Sen. Josh Hawley, a Republican from Missouri, introduced a bill to enact guardrails and prevent the abuse of Flock cameras and similar AI technology.

item.title: Doctor reacts to RFK Jr.'s claim that AI is "better informed" than doctors
item.description: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. says that Americans should consult artificial intelligence rather than a doctor. Dr. Céline Gounder says this is a bad idea.

item.title: Sununu argues "jet fuel has more than doubled" as flight fares soar
item.description: Flight costs have skyrocketed as President Trump's war in Iran causes oil prices to soar. Former New Hampshire Gov. Chris Sununu is the President and CEO of airline lobbying group Airlines for America. Sununu shares his thoughts on high prices and the state of the airline industry.

item.title: "Big Brother" host Julie Chen Moonves and "The Amazing Race" host Phil Keoghan | Between Us
item.description: "Big Brother" host Julie Chen Moonves and "The Amazing Race" host Phil Keoghan talk about their experience leading some of TV's longest-running reality shows.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: "The Amazing Race" and "Big Brother" hosts on being part of long-running TV reality shows
item.description: In a new series called "Between Us," "Big Brother" host Julie Chen Moonves sits down with "The Amazing Race" host Phil Keoghan to discuss their careers on some of television's longest-running reality shows.

item.title: The Dogist announces finalists for People's "World's Cutest Rescue Dog" contest
item.description: Elias Weiss Friedman, known as the Dogist on social media, joins "CBS Mornings" to announce the top three finalists for People's "World's Cutest Rescue Dog" contest. Winners will be announced on Oct. 19.

item.title: Tips for dealing with fall allergies
item.description: Dr. Tania Elliott, a dual board-certified internist and immunologist, joins "CBS Mornings" to offer tips on dealing with fall allergies.

item.title: Teacherless, AI-driven school opens in Chicago
item.description: Chicago's first AI-driven school, called "Alpha," opened this month. Ash-har Quraishi gets an inside look.

item.title: U.S. withdraws from Iraq, declaring an end to major anti-ISIS operation
item.description: Two decades after Operation Inherent Resolve began, U.S. troops have finally withdrawn from Iraq. CBS News' Eleanor Watson reports.

item.title: Witness video shows chaos inside Israel-bound plane before emergency landing
item.description: Disturbing new video shows chaos inside an Israel-bound commercial plane after the pilots allegedly got into an altercation inside the cockpit. CBS News' Dov Lieber has the latest details.

item.title: Van Gogh painting not seen in decades could fetch $180 million at auction
item.description: Several paintings, from a fabled private collection by late Argentine art collectors, could fetch half a billion dollars in total on Nov. 18.

item.title: DA in Cornell case says he never saw interview transcript
item.description: Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten says he never saw a transcript of a conversation between an alleged rape victim and investigators showing what she told Cornell University campus police before his office decided not to bring charges.

item.title: Trump says vague AI agreement is "almost like a constitution," tells tech giants self-regulate
item.description: President Trump and major artificial intelligence executives signed a "morally binding" safety agreement. CBS News' Aaron Navarro explains the contents of the agreement.

item.title: Transcript shows campus police's interview with Jane Doe in Cornell rape case
item.description: We're getting new insight into how Cornell University Police handled the case of an alleged fraternity gang rape back in 2024.

item.title: Treasury to auto-enroll up to 60 million children in Trump Accounts
item.description: Parents will no longer have to sign up for a Trump Account to get one for their child, with auto-enrollment beginning Oct. 1.

item.title: Hawley unveils bill aimed at stopping Flock camera abuse
item.description: Sen. Josh Hawley is unveiling legislation to establish guardrails for Flock cameras and other artificial intelligence-powered surveillance technology, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Critics dubbed it the "anti-transparency bill." A new high-speed rail watchdog report tests that claim.
item.description: A watchdog report on wasteful consultant travel became a real-world test of the so-called high-speed rail "anti-transparency" law.

item.title: Backpack voted Fat Bear Week 2026 winner, beating former champ's offspring
item.description: Voters were split between bear 910 and 89 Backpack in the final round of the weeklong contest to see who is the chunkiest bear at Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska.

item.title: Hegseth directs military academies to stop giving tenure to civilian professors
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered institutions like the Military Academy at West Point and the Naval Academy in Annapolis to stop granting tenure to civilian faculty, in his latest change to military higher education.

item.title: Critics dub it "anti-transparency." A California High-Speed Rail watchdog report reveals otherwise.
item.description: A watchdog report on wasteful consultant travel became a real-world test of the so-called high-speed rail "anti-transparency" law.
